name: Hana Patel

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am from the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to employers, AI companies, unions, parties or government. Your answers are confidential. What is an ordinary day like at your accounting firm?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: The nursery's plant sales arrive as a tidy total, then the returned seedlings turn up in a second file and spoil it. I lead the tax team, prepare the accounts and returns, and enjoy tracing one return to the real sale; what wears me out is a client sending a revised spreadsheet after I have already closed the file. I am 43, with a master's degree and a chartered accountancy qualification. I use AI now and then to draft a list of questions for the nursery owner, but I check each question against the ledger.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If AI does only small routine jobs, the nursery still has to explain its returned plants. A question list might be faster, but I would still check the original sales.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the team that a draft is only a draft, and the named accountant signs the return. I would tell the nursery owner exactly which entries we need explained.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I am paid above the usual rate for this job and we have about eight months of expenses saved. My partner Ben's bus-depot scheduling wage and mine cover the mortgage and our two school-age children, and there are plenty of similar firms nearby.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep preparing the nursery accounts and using approved AI question drafts occasionally, with a check against the ledger before anything goes to the client. I would ask the team to note returned plants separately on the current paid rota, not buy a new system for a small saving.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about our work and money in this picture. The nursery's paperwork is irritating, not a threat to our home.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why separate the returns?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The same seedling can appear as a sale and a refund in different months. I want the client to see which one moved the tax total.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you change firms for more pay?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could, since several firms are nearby, but I like my team and a new title is not a reason to interrupt the children's week. I would need a real written offer first.

say: I would keep a **named accountant** on each return.
I would explain the **returned plants** behind a changed tax total.
think: Our **eight-month reserve** and high pay make the mild case manageable.
Several local firms provide **options**, but I value the current team.
do: Keep **paid nursery accounts** and check occasional approved AI question drafts against the ledger.
Record **returned plants** separately on the existing paid rota.
feel: I feel **calm** about our work and money.
S0.quote: The nursery's paperwork is irritating, not a threat to our home.
fieldNote: Her occasional approved AI use remains a **drafting aid** controlled by the original nursery ledger.
High pay, two wages, many nearby firms and an **eight-month reserve** support calm without forcing a job change.

steps.text: Keep paid nursery returns and record returned plants while checking approved AI question drafts

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If AI starts checking and writing most of our returns, the nursery file could need fewer paid preparers. Robots will reach physical nursery jobs more slowly; the accounting desk changes first.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the partners to show staff the error log and the staffing plan, not just the time saved. I would ask the team to report false matches on paid time.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My own lead hours might be cut if one person can check more clients, even if my tax judgment is strong. Eight months of savings is useful, but Ben's depot wage cannot replace my higher salary and cover the mortgage alone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask my manager Noor for a two-week paid test of anonymised nursery returns against the signed originals, only with written approval. If the test passes, I would learn the approved checker on paid time and use it on live files only after written sign-off; if refused, I would keep the paid manual review while offered. If my hours fall in the first year, I would take a posted senior tax job only with written wage, hours and start date covering the mortgage and a confirmed school pickup plan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about my own hours, although I am willing to test a useful tool. I want the error log before anyone tells us the team is too large.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who checks the test?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Noor and I would count false refund matches and sign the result against the originals. I would not accept a smooth-sounding explanation as evidence.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could Ben collect the children?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My partner Ben would check actual depot shifts before agreeing to a different pickup. A possible shift swap is not a confirmed arrangement.

fieldNote: She is open to tested AI but requires **written approval**, signed results and paid learning before changing live work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: AGI by 2028 could do almost every thinking part of our tax file, including the difficult explanation. Robots around 2031 are later for nursery handling and depot work, but our desk is exposed in 2028.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the firm for written notice and severance terms, and ask the professional association to make those terms public. I would tell the team not to promise a client's file is safe because a person still presses submit.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect the partners to remove my senior post when AGI makes the return so cheaply. Ben's wage would not cover the mortgage alone; eight months of cash gives us time, but I have lain awake wondering what happens at month nine.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would postpone the planned garden room and deposit its monthly budget into job-loss cash while my salary arrives. I would keep every paid tax file offered before any dismissal; in the first year after 2028, if my post ends, I would use the reserve for bills while seeking posted finance-controller roles at local nurseries. I would take a role only with written wage, hours and start date covering the mortgage and actual pickup, knowing that its desk work faces AGI too.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed because I expect to lose our larger wage. A garden room can wait; the next mortgage payment cannot.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would a nursery finance role be safer?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Not automatically; it is also accounts and planning on a screen. An actual paid vacancy would be a bridge, not a claim that the plants protect the desk.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you ask family for help?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would not ask for money while we have savings. I might ask my sister Amira for pickup only if a new job's confirmed hours clash with Ben's actual depot rota.

say: I would seek **written notice and severance** through the association.
I would warn that **2028 desk AGI** arrives before capable robots.
think: I expect my **senior tax post** to end when AGI cuts preparation fees.
Our **eight-month reserve** cannot replace my high wage forever.
do: Postpone the **garden room** and deposit its monthly budget while wages continue.
Keep **paid tax files** while offered; after dismissal use the reserve for bills during search.
Take **posted nursery work** only with written mortgage pay, hours, start and pickup; ask my sister only for confirmed clashes.
feel: I feel **alarmed** by expected loss of our larger wage.
S2.quote: A garden room can wait; the next mortgage payment cannot.
fieldNote: She expects **2028 desk displacement** before capable robots affect the physical nursery or depot.
The nursery controller job is a **conditional paid bridge**, and new deposits come from a postponed planned expense rather than retained savings.

steps.text: Postpone garden room and deposit its monthly budget while wages continue
Keep paid tax files until dismissal; then use reserve for bills during search
After loss take posted nursery finance role with written mortgage-covering wage hours start confirmed pickup
Ask sister for pickup only if confirmed new hours clash with actual depot rota

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years would let me see whether owners pay for a human to untangle returns after AGI drafts them. The tax desk changes in 2031, while capable robots reach hands-on work around 2034.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask our partners to post a paid client-review position with a wage, not offer lunchtime demonstrations. I would tell colleagues we need a real job description before we buy qualifications.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The preparation fee may fall, but I can build a record of solving the nursery's disputed refunds while I am still paid. I would not fund a course from the household reserve just to put another line on my CV.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would take one supervised nursery-owner review each quarter only if Noor assigns it on paid time and the client agrees to a bill. I would read the professional body's free client-dispute notes while keeping paid returns; if the firm posts a defined review job, pays the course fee and gives paid study hours, I would enrol in the client-advice course. Before or after 2031, I would take that posted job only with written wage, hours and start date covering our mortgage and confirmed pickup; if returns end first, I would use the reserve for bills during the search.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious because paid returns may disappear, but five years lets me find out whether clients actually buy review time. A kind client is not a funded post.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if Noor cannot give paid reviews?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep paid tax files while offered and read the free notes. I would not volunteer a quarterly meeting and then call it a new salary.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could Ben alter his hours?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My partner Ben would need a confirmed depot rota before we change school pickup. I would check that alongside a written job offer, not after accepting it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ten years would let us reduce the mortgage while the accounting desk still pays, though AGI reaches it in 2036. Robots around 2039 are later for hands-on work and do not extend tax preparation.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the partners to publish the wage and start date for any client-review role. I would tell the team that a written path is better than an honorary 'future adviser' badge.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think the return-preparation fee may still disappear, but our high pay and eight months saved let us plan rather than jump. I want a smaller loan so a future wage can cover it more easily.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would pay an extra seventy from my monthly paycheque toward principal only if the lender confirms no penalty and normal bills are covered; if there is a penalty, I would deposit it as cash only after normal bills are covered. I would keep paid nursery accounts while offered and take a posted client-review role before or after 2036 only with written wage, hours and start date covering the remaining mortgage and a confirmed family rota. If the accounts end first in the year after 2036, I would use the reserve for bills while seeking that offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about losing the familiar tax desk eventually, but the longer period gives us a workable loan plan. An honorary badge will not make a mortgage payment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you stop working before 2036?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, I am 43 and the children still need us. The cash reserve is for an interruption, not an early retirement plan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the lender charges a fee?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Then I would put the seventy into cash, not pay a penalty to reduce the loan. I would check the regular mortgage and food first.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because it could end my larger wage before we have tested a paid client-review role. Written notice, a real posted job and funded paid training for its duties would help us use the eight-month reserve wisely.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask who tells a client the AGI return was wrong after filing. I want the correction work named on the invoice, with a person who is paid to do it.

headlineQuote: I want the correction work named on the invoice, with a person who is paid to do it.
portrait: Hana is a **43-year-old senior accountant** with a master's and chartered qualification who leads nursery tax work.
Her **high pay**, eight-month reserve, mortgage and many nearby firms provide options while two children depend on wages.
She uses AI **occasionally** and wants a signed comparison before live deployment.
She tests **billed client reviews** and takes courses only with funded fees and paid study time.
biggestWorry: The **2028 AGI** scenario could end her larger wage before a paid review role is proven.
whatWouldHelp: She wants **written notice**, a posted job and funded paid training for defined duties.
